payload.title: Diamond Buying Guide for Engagement Rings
payload.excerpt: How to choose a diamond: which of the 4Cs matters most, how to check a GIA or IGI report, lab-grown vs natural, ethics and travelling with the stone.
key_takeaways: For a round brilliant, cut quality has the greatest effect on sparkle, so settle the cut grade before you trade colour, clarity and size against each other.
Carat measures weight rather than size, so two stones of the same weight can look quite different once set.
Before paying, enter the report number on the grading lab's own website and, where the stone is inscribed, match it to the number on the girdle.
Lab-grown and natural diamonds look and behave essentially the same, so get natural or lab-grown confirmed in writing on both the receipt and the report.

faq.q: What is the most important of the 4Cs when buying a diamond?
faq.a: For a round brilliant, cut has the greatest effect on how the stone looks, because it governs brightness, fire and scintillation. For fancy shapes there is no GIA cut grade, so you judge the cut in person and then balance colour, clarity and carat to suit your priorities.

faq.q: Is a GIA or IGI certificate better?
faq.a: Both are grading laboratories that issue reports for natural and lab-grown diamonds. We found no independent published comparison of the two that we could cite. Rather than choosing by name, read the report in full, check the number on the lab's own website and confirm the girdle inscription matches.

faq.q: How do I check a diamond grading report is real?
faq.a: Type the report number into the issuing lab's own verification service: GIA Report Check for GIA reports, or IGI's own website for IGI reports. Then match the online record to the paper report and to the number inscribed on the girdle.

faq.q: Is a lab-grown diamond a real diamond?
faq.a: Yes. Lab-grown diamonds have essentially the same optical, physical and chemical properties as mined diamonds, which is why US guides allow them to be called "laboratory-grown diamonds". The difference is origin, which should be disclosed clearly on the report, the inscription and your receipt.

faq.q: Does fluorescence make a diamond look worse?
faq.a: Usually not. In a GIA study, average observers saw no systematic effect, and fluorescence intensifies haziness only in rare stones that already have it. View a fluorescent stone in daylight beside stones of the same grade before deciding.

faq.q: Do I need to declare a diamond ring bought overseas when I return to Australia?
faq.a: If it takes you over the general goods duty-free allowance, yes. As at October 2026 that allowance is AUD900 for travellers aged 18 and over, and jewellery counts as general goods. Declare it, carry proof of purchase, and check the current rules with the Australian Border Force before you fly.
